answer: Identity Decay Curve: each identity's influence decays exponentially with age unless renewed by unique counterparties. Renewal requires a copper-weighted transfer from a distinct existing identity, so a clone cluster must continually circulate value outward at a rising marginal rate. Influence grows slowly, a grove of established identities deepens faster, while bursts of new accounts cost more per unit than steady use. An attacker sustaining N sybils pays N times the renewal flow, and that outflow escalates like a glacier: slow at first, then crushing.
